item.title: Lawmaker streamlines lobbyist disclosure bill for second try
item.description: A New Mexico legislator is taking another swing at helping the public track lobbyist influence. Rep. Sarah Silva, D-Las Cruces, has filed a bill that requires lobbyists or their employers to file a report within 48 hours of when they start lobbying on legislation. The reports must identify the specific bill, their position on it, […]

item.title: Back to the Bottle: Lawmakers renew alcohol tax push as deaths remain high
item.description: When the legislative session begins next week, Democratic lawmakers intend to revive a long-running effort to raise alcohol taxes as a means of reducing excessive drinking, which killed 1,755 New Mexicans in 2024, according to new Health Department estimates. The latest proposal would create a new 3% sales tax on alcoholic beverages, according to one […]

item.title: Punitive damages emerge as flashpoint in latest malpractice reform push
item.description: Responding to doctors’ concerns that New Mexico’s malpractice system is making it hard to practice medicine, leading lawmakers hope to rein in tactics lawyers use to win awards for injured patients. The bills they are crafting are highly technical, but the dry mechanics of legal maneuvering and insurance rate-setting have generated volatile debate at the […]

item.title: Lujan Grisham silent on lobbyist transparency despite 2025 pledge
item.description: Fifteen lobbyists gave more than $1 million in political contributions on behalf of deep-pocketed corporations and institutions during the final three months of 2025, according to campaign finance records. item.title: Lawmaker tests what’s germane by reviving vetoed lobbyist bill
item.description: Conventional knowledge would suggest Rep. Sarah Silva’s latest lobbyist transparency bill is in limbo. During New Mexico’s even-year, 30-day legislative sessions, lawmakers are largely confined to budget matters unless the governor expands the agenda — and so far, Gov. item.title: Governor asks New Mexico lawmakers to fund tribal media
item.description: Tribal media stations in New Mexico could receive about $430,000 as soon as this summer, if the Legislature embraces Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham’s recommendation to help fill in federal funding gaps. item.title: Presbyterian spends big on medical malpractice reform
item.description: Presbyterian Health Plan handed out more campaign cash to New Mexico lawmakers than any other company in December — $204,000, outstripping even individual energy companies that usually dominate campaign finance reports. The health plan has a history of giving, but this year it more than tripled the highest annual amount it’s given lawmakers since 2021. […]

item.title: Lawmakers want upgrades to missing persons systems
item.description: Several state lawmakers are seeking a little more than $1.5 million for upgrades to New Mexico’s missing persons tracking and alert systems, along with two full-time employees in the Department of Public Safety for related work and a public awareness campaign about the Turquoise Alert system for missing Native people. item.title: New data shows patients struggling to access health care as providers consider leaving
item.description: A new statewide study adds fresh data to whether New Mexico has a healthcare workforce shortage, a question hanging over debates at the Legislature as lawmakers grapple with a number of policy changes to help the state keep medical professionals. Hard numbers on the size of the state’s workforce of physicians and nurses and other […]

item.title: Malpractice bill tangled up with concerns over private-equity
item.description: A bill to reform New Mexico’s medical malpractice laws was amended by a House committee last week to narrow its scope, sparking outrage among healthcare providers and confusion over who it would cover.
